Text: This wavekin's vibrant flanks call to mind the iridescent strata of Worqor Lar Dor. Indeed, legend has it that the creature began life as a chunk of rock from that mighty edifice that plunged into a lake after being seized by sudden thirst.
Unknown_70_1: A rainbow-hued form glimmers in the water!
Unknown_70_2: The rainbow glimmer fades from view...
Unknown_70_3: You reel in the rainbow-hued form!

Text: Rimed with algae and wreathed in foliage, this still, silent hunter lurks in the gloomy substrate of Miyakabek'zu. Intriguingly, the crystalline protrusions on its back share the same internal structure as many precious gems.

While Eorzean eyes might associate this wavekin's rounded form with that of a heart, for the Mamool Ja, this revered creature is a symbol of the sky itself─a facet of the firmament glimpsed briefly through the swaying canopy above.

Some naturalists believe─against all evidence to the contrary─that rroneek are in fact a species of fish, and point to this ancient horned wavekin as some kind of progenitor. Regardless of one's thoughts on the matter, the creature's horns certainly evoke their land-dwelling namesake.

Formed when lesser balls of lightning collide and fuse, these colossal, coruscating specimens are exceptionally volatile. The slightest rupture in its outer membrane can result in a catastrophic discharge of levin─a phenomenon which has left more than one curious naturalist frazzled...or worse.

Endowed with three curving, scythe-like fins, this terrifying wavekin is the culmination of experiments to replicate an ancient sea monster. When its creators discovered it could cleave through electrope with unsettling ease, they began to regret their success.
